t: That section 102(c)(1) of the Renegotiation Act of 1951, as amended (50 U.S.C. App., sec. 1212(c)(1)), is amended by striking out “June 30, 1966” and inserting in lieu thereof “June 30, 1968”.

fable.w: This section only extends a termination date in the Renegotiation Act of 1951 by replacing one date with another. A tempting reading is that the Renegotiation Act involves contractors dealing with the government, but nothing in this text creates or requires consultation, hearings, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. It is a purely technical date amendment.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “June 30, 1966” and inserting in lieu thereof “June 30, 1968”

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple amendment to a statutory deadline. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. It merely changes a date within the law.
qwen_block.s: That section 102(c)(1) of the Renegotiation Act of 1951, as amended (50 U.S.C. App., sec. 1212(c)(1)), is amended by striking out “June 30, 1966” and inserting in lieu thereof “June 30, 1968”.

opus.w: This section only changes a date in the Renegotiation Act of 1951, replacing June 30, 1966 with June 30, 1968. It sets up no hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue. One could argue that renegotiation itself means dealing with private contractors. But that process is not described here, and renegotiating a contract is closer to a contract matter than to outside participation in a federal policy decision.
opus.s: is amended by striking out “June 30, 1966” and inserting in lieu thereof “June 30, 1968”.

There is no interaction with non-federal entities described in this text.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a date in a statute could affect future participation processes, but the text itself contains no mechanism for public input, consultation, or advisory involvement. It is purely a technical amendment to a deadline.
